title: Chat timeout_s never reaches HTTP client

answer.patch:
--- a/chat/wrap.py
+++ b/chat/wrap.py
@@ -16,12 +16,12 @@ def chat_wrapped(
     max_tokens: int = 1024,
     retry: int = 1,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    del timeout_s
     last: dict[str, Any] | None = None
     for _ in range(max(1, retry)):
         last = api.post_chat(
             model,
             messages,
+            timeout_s=timeout_s,
             temperature=temperature,
             max_tokens=max_tokens,
         )
answer.reason: In chat/wrap.py, chat_wrapped() receives timeout_s but discards it with `del timeout_s` and never passes it to api.post_chat(). The fix removes the `del` and forwards timeout_s to the HTTP layer.

title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@ def subprocess_with_hard_timeout(
         proc.wait(timeout=10)
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if str(stdout).strip() or str(stderr).strip():
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                 args=cmd,
                 returncode=-9,
answer.reason: Line 59 only checks stdout for content. When a subprocess writes only to stderr, stdout is empty, the condition is False, and the code raises ProcTimeout on line 66, losing the stderr diagnostics. Changed the condition to also check stderr so that a CompletedProcess is returned whenever either stream has output.

title: Warmup ignores short timeout

answer.patch:
--- a/warmup.py
+++ b/warmup.py
@@ -11,3 +11,3 @@
 def warmup(model: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
     _ = config.FIRST_BYTE_S
-    return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK")
+    return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK", timeout_s=config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S)
answer.reason: warmup() calls chat() without a timeout_s argument, so it inherits the suite's FIRST_BYTE_S budget (default 600s). The config already defines DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S (default 30s) but it is never used in the warmup path. Adding timeout_s=config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S ensures warmup fails fast (~30s) instead of waiting up to 600s against a wedged backend.
